_README: Gates in this directory that have no <gate>.test.mjs, each with the reason it does not yet.
This list is a WORK QUEUE, not an amnesty. validate-gates-have-tests.mjs fails if an entry
names a gate that has since gained a test, or a gate that no longer exists, so the list can
only shrink. Each reason says which of three things is true, because they are not the same
problem and do not cost the same to fix:
CHEAP        the gate takes its input by CLI flag or exported function and a few small
fixture files would drive it red today. ALL FIVE ARE NOW DONE (2026-09-18,
84 tests, 35 mutations proven) and their entries are gone from this list.
NEEDS ROOT   the gate hardcodes resolve(__dirname, '../..') with no env override, so a
fixture tree cannot be substituted. The fix is one line per gate, copying
the CONTENT_REVIEW_GATE_ROOT / PAYMENT_GATE_ROOT / ANALYTICS_GATE_ROOT
pattern already used by four gates here. Writing the harness means changing
the gate, which is a separate decision from writing a test.
NEEDS LIVE   the gate's only input is a live remote D1 read through wrangler with real
credentials, with no injectable query function and no local fixture path.
Hermetic falsification is not reachable without a seam being added first.
Written 2026-09-18, when this gate was added. 12 of 27 gates had a harness, all four of
them written that same day, and the audit that prompted it found the other 15 had never
been watched fail. Do not add an entry here to make a red run green: a gate you are
shipping is a gate you can test.
UPDATE 2026-09-18, same day: the five CHEAP gates were harnessed and removed from this
list, taking it from 15 entries to 10. Writing them turned up three defects the gates
could not see, each pinned as a failing-state test naming it rather than fixed in a
harness PR: abstract-snippet.mjs over-strips prose before a colon (860 of 3,720
abstracts, 29,935 characters), validate-email-trickle ET4 matches a prefixed constant
name for want of a word boundary, and validate-no-unfinished-copy applies its
allowlist per FILE so one entry disables all six rules there. compare-pillar-migration
also silently skips its guides.json leg on a partial flag set while still printing
", guides.json" in the success line.

gates.check-removed-ids.mjs: NEEDS ROOT, and a git seam besides. Its input is execSync('git diff --cached'), hardcoded with no cwd or diff-source parameter, so a fixture must be a real git repo with a real staged change. parseDiff, extractRemovedIds, idStillPresentInFile and grepConsumers are each separately callable and testable today, which is the way in.
gates.validate-email-verification.mjs: NEEDS ROOT. Three auth files read through resolve(__dirname, '../..') with no env override. Worth doing early despite that: its three gates guard a magic-link token against truncation and replay, which is the highest-consequence assertion in this directory and the one whose silent weakening would be hardest to notice.
gates.validate-share-button.mjs: NEEDS ROOT. Four pure regex gates over two hardcoded paths under resolve(__dirname, '../..'), so a fixture tree would have to reproduce src/pages/library/[...slug].astro and src/components/ArticleHero.astro at those exact paths. One override line turns this into a CHEAP entry.
gates.validate-guides-registry.mjs: NEEDS ROOT, more than one line of it. ROOT, SSOT_PATH and a hardcoded six-entry CONSUMERS list all resolve off __dirname, and gateG5 additionally reads a SIBLING repo (../rrm-router/src/index.js), silently skipping when absent, which is its own untested branch. gateG7 already accepts an injectable readFile, so the pattern is half established.
gates.validate-infographic-svg.mjs: NEEDS ROOT in the form of module injection, not a path. It imports SAMPLES, renderInfographic, ASPECTS and houseStyleErrors as static ESM specifiers, so a fixture spec set cannot be substituted without editing src/lib/infographic/. It is otherwise fully hermetic (no network, no D1), so a seam here is cheaper than most.
gates.verify-library-curation.mjs: NEEDS ROOT, and a build. Every path is a bare relative string resolved from cwd, and four of them live in dist/, so the gate only means anything after npm run build. A fixture can be a hand-built dist/ tree, which is the point of testing it, but it also statically imports the real src/data/library-topics.ts for CATEGORIES and DEMOTED_SLUGS.
gates.validate-glossary-pipeline.mjs: NEEDS ROOT for G1 to G5 and a fetch seam for G6. The five static gates read fixed paths under resolve(__dirname, '../..') and walk src/, so they are ordinary once a root override lands. G6 fetches the live production pillar with no injectable fetch and WARN-skips on failure, which is a gate that goes quiet exactly when the network does.
gates.validate-courses-schema.mjs: NEEDS LIVE for CS2 and CS4, NEEDS ROOT for CS1 and CS3. The static half compares duplicated enum Sets against committed CHECK constraints and is testable behind one override line. CS2 and CS4 shell out to wrangler d1 execute --remote against rrm-auth and WARN-skip when it is unreachable, so today they are silently absent in any environment without Cloudflare credentials, CI included.
gates.validate-quiz-parity.mjs: NEEDS LIVE. d1Query hardcodes the rrm-auth database name and shells out to wrangler d1 execute --remote unconditionally, with no injectable query function and, unlike the courses gate, no catch, so it throws rather than skipping. Its scoring-divergence check is genuinely valuable and genuinely unreachable hermetically until a query seam exists.
gates.validate-glossary-publish-ready.mjs: NEEDS LIVE, completely. It reads no local file at all: both queries go to live rrm-auth through wrangler, and credentials come from CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN or a 1Password read. There is no database-name override and no fixture path, so its 10 review-artifact patterns cannot be falsified without either a seam or a real D1 holding planted rows.
